questions.question: Name and describe five types of sheet metal defects.
questions.idealAnswer: 1. Burnishing- a polishing caused by two surfaces sliding together with a hard or smooth surface, usually there is no removal of metal. 2. Crack- A physical separation of two adjacent portions of metal. Evidence of a crack, a thin line across the surface, a few thousands of an inch to completely through the metal caused by excessive stress. 3. Dent- Indentation of the metal surface produced by an object striking with force. The surface around the indentation is usually slightly upset. 4. Inclusion-Presence of foreign or extraneous material wholly with in a portion of the material. Inclusions are introduced during manufacturing process. 5. Score- deeper than a scratch, tear or break in the metal that results from contact under pressure. May show discoloration from temperature do to friction. Other defects are Brinelling, Burr, Corrosion, Cut, Erosion, Chattering, Galling, Gouge, Nick, Pitting, Scratch, Stain and Upsetting.

questions.question: What is involved in the selection of repair material?
questions.idealAnswer: The repair material must duplicate the original strength of the the structure. The same type material and thickness is desired. When same type and thickness is not available one heavier gauge may be used as long as the material is the same type. Never ever use material that is weaker or thinner than original. Also repairs that are made too strong will cause the structure to be weaker than the the surrounding repair and cause stress points at the end of the repair, that could lead to structural damage later. The aircraft is designed is such a way that it must be somewhat flexible while taking off landing and flight maneuvers.

questions.question: When forming a bend in material what is K- factor and how is it used?
questions.idealAnswer: The K- factor is the percentage of material thickness where there is no stretching or compressing (shrinking) of the material, (neutral axis) the percentage has been calculated as one of the (179) numbers on the k-chart. The number corresponds to the angle at witch the metal is bent. The k-factor for 90 degree bend is 1, all others degrees must use the k-factor to calculate Setback. The K- factor is multiplied by the sum of material thickness and bend radius to arrive at the setback of the bend.

questions.question: How is a rivet selected for a repair?
questions.idealAnswer: Normally the rivet size should be the same size as original rivets in the part being repaired. If however, the rivet hole is enlarged or deformed the next larger rivet diameter should be used. Rivet diameter can also be determined by looking at adjacent rows made by the manufacturer next to repair (inboard on wing or forward on fuselage) Another method is to multiply the thickness of the thickest sheet by three. The number of rivets can be found in the structural repair manual of the manufacture of the specific aircraft or using the AC43:13-1B

questions.question: What actions are taken to install a rivet?
questions.idealAnswer: Transferring and preparing original hole, drilling and driving rivets. Holes must be correctly located. Accomplish transfer of holes from a drilled part to another part by placing one part over the other using original holes as a guide. A scribe can also be used to transfer holes from the drilled part. Make sure to use the correct size drill bit for the the rivet being used. All burrs and chips must be removed. Make sure to use the proper size clecos to be sure all the holes line up perfectly. When riveting with a partner make sure to communicate using a code 1knock, 2Knocks, 3knocks and inspect the rivet shop head for proper width and height. Also check for looseness and proper installation.

questions.question: What are some precautions when working with Magnesium, CRES and Titanium?
questions.idealAnswer: When working with corrosion resistant steel (CRES) a finish must be applied or it will cause corrosion to other metals when mated together. Also a lager bend radius must be selected to prevent cracking. Magnesium and titanium particles can easily ignite so work with these materials far away from any ignition source. If a fire does breakout use dry talc, calcium carbonate, sand and graphite to extinguish both magnesium and titanium fires. Do not use water, foam, carbon tetrachloride or carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What are safety precautions when operating a drill press?
questions.idealAnswer: Wear eye and ear protection, clamp the workpiece securely, adjust for the proper RPM, stop machine completely before adjusting workpiece and clean the area when finished.

questions.question: What is a lightening hole?
questions.idealAnswer: Lightening holes are cut into rib sections, fuselage frames, and other structural parts to decrease weight. Flanges are pressed around the holes for strength.
